messages.subject_clean: What processing steps (for MSStatsTMT) are required for output from Trans Proteomics Pipeline?
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone

I am using Trans proteomics pipeline for TMT based analysis. Unfortunately, I have not come across any converter for the same. Please guide me on what processing steps are required. Here are the ones I could guess from other converters:

Peptide ions which are shared by more than one protein to be removed
If one spectrum has multiple identifications within one run, it only keeps the best identification with the minimal number of missing reporter ion intensities, highest reporter ion intensity, or lowest interference score if the information was available
If a spectrum only has one or two reporter ion intensities within one MS run, it removes the spectrum from that run
Ambiguous protein groups which contained multiple proteins were filtered out
For fractionation, If a peptide ion was shared by multiple fractions, we kept the fraction with maximal average reporter ion abundance across all the channel in the fraction.
Do I need to ADD any other processing steps? Please let me know.

Regards
Debojyoti
PhD Student

messages.subject_clean: Inquiry Regarding MSstatsPTM Usage and Normalization Methodology
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

To normalize your data for label free quantification proteomics data using MSstatsPTM, you can use the `normalization` and `normalization.PTM` parameters.  `normalization` corresponds to the first experiment that uses label free quantification strategy and `normalization.PTM` corresponds to the second experiment that performs quantification of methylation modifications based on enrichment strategy.  This link <https://rdrr.io/github/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsPTM/man/dataSummarizationPTM.html> should provide more information on those parameters.

The example below represents equalizing medians normalization for both experiments:

summarized_data = dataSummarizationPTM( data, normalization = "equalizeMedians", normalization.PTM = "equalizeMedians", )

Using the output from the previous code, you can run the below code to validate if normalization was applied correctly (see link <https://rdrr.io/github/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsPTM/man/dataProcessPlotsPTM.html> for details):

dataProcessPlotsPTM( summarized_data, type = "QCPlot", )

Please let me know if you have any more questions or if I misinterpreted your question.

Thanks,
Tony

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm a little confused from your statement that "the data typically used in MSstatsPTM is from a single search result".

I believe the data used in MSstatsPTM is typically from two separate searches.  If you look at Fig. 3 of this paper <https://www.mcponline.org/article/S1535-9476(22)00285-7/fulltext> on MSstatsPTM, you can see that identification and quantification for the first and second experiments happen separately and independently of each other.

So given you have 2 datasets, we can use the MaxQuant converter function to take your 2 datasets and transform it into msstatsPTM format.  Pay attention to the two parameters `evidence_prot` and `annotation_protein`, which is where you input your dataset from the first label free experiment.  `evidence` and `annotation` parameters are used for your enriched dataset.

msstatsptm_format = MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat(evidence=dataset_enriched, annotation=dataset_enriched_annotation,
evidence_prot=dataset_label_free,
annotation_protein=dataset_label_free_annotation, fasta_path="fasta_file_from_uniprot.fasta")

Let me know if you have any more questions or if I didn't interpret your question correctly.

Thanks,
Tony

messages.body_plain:
Hi Giovanni,

We actually perform the analysis a little differently than how you describe above.

For DIA we take each individual fragment as feature which represents the underlying protein abundance (i.e., we are not grouping feature by peptides). All of these features are used individually and summarized using Tukey's Median Polish (similar to median summarization) in the dataProcess function.

In terms of feature selection (removing features with interferences/missing values/ect) there are a couple options. In the dataProcess function you can choose to use all fragments, the top N fragments (based on average intensity), or have MSstats select the "best" features using an internal selection algorithm. There is more info on these options in Box 2 of our new MSstats paper : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01000-3.

Hope this helps!

Devon

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using MSstats to process a large DDA dataset (some conditions have only one biological replicate that I will do a separate analysis on just to look for presence/absence of proteins, but for most of the dataset there are four conditions at 8 different times - not repeated measures with 3-4 bioReps for most samples and some samples with technical reps) that was first processed by maxQuant.

 I ran dataProcess() using the following and it seemingly worked great (output message attached in 'dataProcess.output'):

quant.maxquant <- dataProcess(input.maxquant logTrans = 2,
normalization='equalizeMedians',
summaryMethod="TMP",
cutoffCensored="minFeature", censoredInt="NA",
MBimpute=TRUE,
maxQuantileforCensored=0.999)

However, I had a lot of missing data and so was worried about the imputation:
dim(quant.maxquant$RunlevelData) #68928
sum(quant.maxquant$RunlevelData$more50missing==TRUE) # 59903
sum(quant.maxquant$RunlevelData$more50missing==FALSE) # 9025

and so I decided to run processData again with remove50missing=TRUE, but when I did, I did not get any RunLevelData in the output.

Here is what I ended up running:
quant.maxquant.rm50 <- dataProcess(input.maxquant, logTrans = 2,
normalization='equalizeMedians',
summaryMethod="TMP",
cutoffCensored="minFeature", censoredInt="NA",
MBimpute=TRUE,
maxQuantileforCensored=0.999,remove50missing=TRUE)

The standard output of dataProcess() is attached as a text file here in 'dataProcess.rm50.output'.

head(quant.maxquant.rm50$RunlevelData)
Null

Any help would be much appreciated!

Thanks,
Nadia
